title: Benchmark harness: add end-to-end streaming chat scenario (TTFT/TPOT + phase breakdown)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Add an end-to-end benchmark scenario to the benchmark harness that exercises *streaming chat* (hosted-like traffic shape) and produces defensible TTFT/TPOT and per-phase timing breakdowns for quantized (FP8/INT8) vs FP16 paths.

Why
Our current harness is strong on microbench + non-streaming throughput, but we’re missing the user-facing metrics that regress in practice under quant + scheduler interactions:
- TTFT (time to first token): prefill + queueing + scheduler behavior
- TPOT (time per output token): steady-state decode + batching efficiency

This scenario is a sprint deliverable and is a gating input for quant perf canary + the sprint report.

Scope
- Scenario: streaming chat completion, with token streaming enabled, producing TTFT + TPOT, plus breakdown of:
  - client->server request overhead (optional if measurable)
  - queue wait time (if available via runtime instrumentation)
  - prefill time (prompt processing)
  - decode time (generation)
- Workloads: must support presets from the “top hosted” model/workload matrix (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy distributions), including realistic concurrency.
- Output: standardized result artifacts (JSON; parquet optional stub) that match the benchmark-lab metadata tagging conventions (model, GPU SKU, quant mode, runtime commit, container digest, run ID).

Non-goals
- Replacing existing microbench suite
- Full-blown prompt/eval correctness testing beyond basic drift guardrails (handled in ENG-24819 / applied ML)

Acceptance criteria
1) New scenario runnable via benchmark-lab CLI:
   - Example: `bench run --scenario streaming_chat --preset <preset> --model <model> --quant <fp16|fp8|int8> --gpu <sku> ...`
   - Supports both single-run and matrix-generated runs.
2) Computes and emits:
   - TTFT (ms): p50/p95/p99 across requests
   - TPOT (ms/token): p50/p95/p99 across requests
   - tokens/sec (aggregate) and request-level token counts
   - Phase breakdown metrics for prefill vs decode (at minimum)
3) Warmup + repetition semantics:
   - Configurable warmup requests excluded from aggregation
   - Configurable repetitions with stable aggregation rules (per ADR)
4) Artifact format:
   - JSON output includes run metadata tags: model family, model id, quant mode, GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, runtime commit, benchmark-lab commit, container digest, region/perf-lab cluster, start/end timestamps.
   - Results include both per-request samples (or summary + optional samples) and summaries for dashboards.
5) Documentation:
   - README / docs page in benchmark-lab describing scenario, required flags, and interpretation caveats (TTFT vs TPOT tradeoff).
6) Rollout plan:
   - Land behind a "scenario" registry entry and keep prior defaults unchanged.
   - Add at least 1 config example that can be consumed by perf-canary nightly (see perf-canary PR) and confirm output is ingestible.

Notes / references
- Metrics definitions: Confluence ADR “quant benchmark metrics and definitions” (TTFT/TPOT aggregation rules)
- Related PRs:
  - benchmark-lab PR #413 (implementation target)
  - benchmark-lab PR #415 (artifact format + tags)
- Owners: Rina (harness), Noah (perf methodology sanity), Sofia/Marcus (scheduler metrics interpretation), Allison (dashboard ingestion)

Implementation sketch
- Use existing chat client in harness with streaming enabled.
- Capture timestamps for:
  - request start
  - first token received
  - completion end
- Derive:
  - TTFT = t_first_token - t_request_start
  - TPOT = (t_end - t_first_token) / (n_output_tokens - 1) [guard for 0/1 token]
- If runtime emits phase timings in structured logs (prefill/decode), parse and attach to request records for breakdowns.

Risks / gotchas
- Client-side measurement noise; must run in perf-lab close to servers to avoid network jitter dominating.
- Streaming backpressure and concurrency can skew TPOT; must define concurrency semantics (fixed number of in-flight requests).
- Beware of counting first token in TPOT denominator; standardize formula per ADR.

Deliverables
- Code in benchmark-lab
- Example config(s) for H100 + A100 baseline
- Sample output artifact checked into docs/tests for schema validation
- Link to a successful perf-lab run for reviewers
comments: 2025-10-01 (Talia Benson): Marking P0 for sprint. We need TTFT/TPOT numbers for the report and perf-canary gating. Please align formulas with ADR; we’ve had confusion in prior readouts re: TPOT denominator.

2025-10-02 (Rina Kobayashi): Drafted the scenario interface. Plan is to emit request-level samples (ttft_ms, tpot_ms_per_token, prompt_tokens, output_tokens) plus aggregated percentiles. Will also add `--warmup-requests` and `--max-inflight` to control concurrency.

2025-10-03 (Noah Patel): Please make sure we can attribute prefill vs decode. Even if we don’t have full per-op timings, at least split (prefill_time_ms, decode_time_ms) from runtime structured perf events when available; otherwise emit "unknown" and keep TTFT/TPOT as primary E2E metrics.

2025-10-04 (Rina Kobayashi): Implemented timestamping around streaming client. Using monotonic clock; first token timestamp is on first non-empty delta. Added guardrails for cases where output_tokens <= 1 (tpot set to "nan" and excluded from TPOT aggregation).

2025-10-06 (Allison Grant): For dashboard ingestion, please ensure tags are consistent with the rest of the suite: `gpu_sku`, `quant_mode`, `runtime_commit`, `container_digest`, `scenario`, `preset`, `model_id`, `model_family`. Also include `run_url` if you have it (perf-lab job link).

2025-10-07 (Rina Kobayashi): Opened benchmark-lab PR #413 with scenario runner + metrics aggregation + docs. Added JSON schema validation and a sample output file for CI. Phase breakdown is populated if runtime perf JSON events are present; otherwise it will be blank and we warn.

2025-10-08 (Marcus Reed): Review note: concurrency semantics should be "max inflight requests" not threads, and we should record effective concurrency observed (avg inflight). Also, please record prompt/output token counts per request to explain TPOT shifts under different decoding params.

2025-10-09 (Rina Kobayashi): Addressed review: renamed to `max_inflight`, added `avg_inflight_observed`, and added per-request token counts. Confirmed outputs are compatible with artifact uploader changes in PR #415. Ran smoke in perf-lab on H100; TTFT/TPOT look sane (TTFT tighter than non-stream due to earlier first-byte).

2025-10-10 (Connor O'Brien): Great—this is now unblocking perf-canary quant job wiring. Once #413 is merged, we’ll reference the config in perf-canary PR #188 and start nightly on H100 + L40S. Marking Done on this issue; follow-ups for any drift in dashboard ingestion can go into ENG-24817.
